metadata.title: One Electron Interferes With Itself
metadata.thing: the single-electron buildup: dots becoming fringes
chapters: What we skipped, and your turn
metadata.long_title: One Electron Interferes With Itself — the double slit, one dot at a time | Bear's Notes
metadata.description_blurb: In this video: the single-electron buildup — 10 random dots, then 200, 6,000, 70,000 — turning into interference fringes; why waves make stripes and particles should make two heaps; each electron's wave passing through both slits and interfering with itself; the dot histogram as |ψ|²; λ = h/p setting the stripe spacing; why watching which slit kills the fringes; and why 2,000-atom molecules show stripes while you, at λ ≈ 10⁻³⁵ m, never will.
metadata.short_blurb: The single-electron double slit, from dots to fringes. Full explainer on the channel.
